rules.statement: The word 'motion', as used in section 91 of the Civil Procedure Code, does not necessarily mean a written motion. Section 408 requires parties to notify their settlement to court by motion, but does not require a written memorandum for settlements under section 408.
rules.supporting_quote: "Further, when parties finally settle their disputes and notify the terms of the compromise to Court, the Court is bound to enter the terms of then' settlement and then pass a decree (vide section 408 of the Civil Procedure Code). This is a step in the course of regular procedure specifically provided for by the Civil Procedure Code and is not a step incidental to the proceedings. Consequently, there is no requirement that section 91 should be complied with when parties enter into a settlement under section 408 of the Civil Procedure Code."
rules.statute_citation_verbatim: section 408 of the Civil Procedure Code
